summary:
Mars Training Academy (M.T.A) is a browser-based game, built in Scratch, that teaches kids ages 7-12 the real trade-offs astronauts face on a Martian outpost. Players manage three competing resources — Oxygen, Energy and Radiation Shield — where no choice is free: pressing O to recover oxygen or S to reinforce the shield both cost precious Energy, which is regained by collecting Mars rock samples.

The game is grounded entirely in real NASA open data. 20 real solar flares, pulled live from the NASA DONKI API (including the powerful X5.8 of May 10, 2024), strike the base and damage the shield based on each flare's real GOES class. The collectible rocks use real sample names cored by NASA's Perseverance rover in Jezero Crater.

It addresses the challenge by turning genuine mission constraints into gameplay a child can feel: every decision teaches something true about surviving in deep space. It matters because it closes the gap between abstract space facts and the real decision-making logic behind a mission.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: Mars Training Academy (M.T.A) is a browser game, built in Scratch, where kids ages 7-12 run a Martian outpost and manage three competing resources: Oxygen, Energy and Radiation Shield. The player walks out of the ship onto Mars, collects real rock samples (press R) to gain Energy, and spends that Energy to recover Oxygen (O) or reinforce the Shield (S). Real solar storms strike the base and damage the shield. Collect every rock to win the mission.

HOW IT WORKS / THE TRADE-OFF: No choice is free. Energy is the bottleneck — spending it on air leaves less for shielding, mirroring real mission planning. This is the core educational mechanic.

REAL NASA DATA: 20 real solar flares pulled live from the NASA DONKI API (two GET requests merged, including the X5.8 of May 10, 2024). Shield damage is derived from each flare's real GOES class. Collectible rocks use real sample names cored by NASA's Perseverance rover in Jezero Crater (Montdenier, Montagnac, Salette, Coulettes, Robine, Malay).

TOOLS: Scratch (block programming). Data from NASA DONKI, Perseverance sample catalog, and Curiosity/Ingenuity Mars imagery.

IMPACT: It closes the gap between abstract space facts and the real decision-making logic behind a mission, so a child walks away understanding a true constraint of deep-space survival.

TEAM: Built by two 11-year-olds and a mentor. AI tools (ChatGPT for the title art, Claude for coding guidance, English text, and fetching/merging the DONKI data) were used as assistance; all design decisions and implementation were made by the team.
